newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MP's condemn U.S. vote on Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MP's condemn U.S. vote on Jerusalem.

text.p: Kuwait's parliament on Saturday condemned a non-binding U.S. House of Representatives resolution calling on President Bill Clinton to reaffirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital.
The chamber also expressed hope that Clinton would not endorse plans to move and open an embassy in Jerusalem, the official news agency KUNA said.
"We regret this decision which we feel will draw the region closer to violence...to an explosion," the MP'S said in a statement issued after a meeting.
"It (the resolution) also hampers the peace process in the Middle East...and heralds the start of a war against the Palestinians".
Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, has welcomed Tuesday's 406-17 vote.

The House vote, which does not oblige the Clinton administration to act, came as Egypt struggled to resolve a peacemaking crisis between Israel and the PLO which erupted when Israel began work in March on a 6,500-home Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestinians, who regard East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state, have termed the resolution a declaration of war.

In October 1995, the U.S. Senate and the House passed the Jerusalem Embassy Act which states as a matter of U.S. policy that Jerusalem should remain "the undivided capital of Israel" and that the American embassy should be moved there by May 1999.
But recognising the volatility of the issue of Jerusalem, it allowed Clinton to suspend the embassy's move from Tel Aviv for six-month periods.
Costa Rica and El Salvador are the only countries with embassies in Jerusalem.
